newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy can reach 3pct deficit goal - undersecretary.
newsitem.headline: Italy can reach 3pct deficit goal - undersecretary.

text.p: Italian budget undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta said on Wednesday that Italy was still in condition to reach a key deficit goal for monetary union, despite a European Commission forecast that it would overshoot.

Macciotta told reporters he expected the government to draw up a 1998 budget of some 20 trillion lire to meet the three percent deficit to Gross Domestic Product goal required for EMU. The Commission forecast a 1997 ratio of 3.2 percent and 3.9 percent for 1998.

The news was a blow to Italy's stringent efforts to qualify for economic and monetary union at its planned 1999 launch, and overshadowed preliminary inflation data this week pointing to an annual rate in April of 1.7 percent, its lowest for 28 years.
But Macciotta said: "I bet that in a month we will have inflation at 1.5 percent."

He said that Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government already knew very well that the deficit-GDP ratio next year could balloon. "That's why the government is expecting to draw up a budget...of around 20 trillion lire," he said.

A decision will be made next May on which EU states qualify for monetary union on the basis of their 1997 performance. "I think Italy is in condition to reach the three percent (goal)," Macciotta said.
